title: NLB/ALB upgrade orchestrator: zero-downtime attach/replace for internal ingress
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) customers running Redwood Private rely on internal LBs (NLB fronting ALB or ALB-only) for tenant ingress. Current Terraform modules replace listeners/target groups in-place which can drop long-lived inference streams (streaming responses, websocket-like clients) and break prefix/KV cached sessions during upgrades. We need an orchestrator Terraform module + migration pattern that enables zero-downtime replacement of LB artifacts, automated health choreography and safe cutover, and repeatable state migration for multiple accounts/regions.

Scope:
- New terraform module: "ingress_orchestrator" that manages pairwise replacement of NLB/ALB listener+target-group resources with atomic cutover steps.
- Support both TLS offload (ACM certs on ALB) and TLS passthrough (NLB TCP/SSL) topologies.
- Connection draining, pre-warm targets, and active health probe choreography across AZs.
- Canary weighted routing using ALB rule priorities and NLB target weights for staged rollouts.
- Migration helpers (state import guidance and automated plan generation script) to avoid manual drift during module adoption.
- Terraform 1.6+ compatibility and clear upgrade path from existing ingress modules.

Non-goals: rearchitecting application-level session handling, replacing customer app behavior for long-lived streams.

Why: This reduces upgrade risk for Private customers, keeps streaming inference sessions alive, and reduces incident fire drills during routine infra upgrades. It also unlocks safer TLS profile changes (e.g., moving from pass-through to offload) and cert rotations with no user-visible interruptions.
acceptance_criteria: Module provides resources to create "new" listener and target groups alongside existing ones and a documented, scripted cutover step that flips traffic without 500/502 spikes.
Automated canary rollout: ability to route N% traffic to new target group and monitor health metrics for a configurable window before shifting remaining traffic.
Health choreography ensures at least 95% of targets report healthy across AZs before traffic shift and auto-rolls back on regression.
Zero packet-loss for long-lived streaming sessions demonstrated in load test (10k simultaneous streaming connections across region) with <0.5% connection resets during cutover.
Terraform plan/import docs and migration script included with clear operator checklist for customers.
Module passes internal security review and includes IAM least-privilege terraform examples for cross-account deployments.
tasks: Design resource graph and state migration strategy (create new listeners+target groups, populate targets, then atomically update routing rules)
Implement terraform module with configurable topology: nlb-only, alb-only, nlb->alb hybrid, tls-passthrough/offload flags
Add automated canary controller script (external tool invoked by ops) to adjust weights and monitor CloudWatch/Datadog metrics
Implement health prober config templates for HTTP/HTTPS/TCP probes with cross-AZ aggregation
Write migration script that: discovers current LB/target group ARNs, generates terraform import commands and a dry-run plan, and produces rollback plan
Create e2e load test harness (k6 + custom streaming client) and run in staging to validate zero-downtime cutover
Documentation: operator runbook, upgrade checklist, terraform examples, and known-issues section
Submit module for security review and incorporate findings
comments: 2026-01-13 — Maya Chen: Kickoff, scoped design review with infra and platform. Drafted resource graph and preliminary cutover sequence. Assigned Rafael as owner.

2026-01-28 — Rafael Gomez: Implemented terraform module skeleton: supports "topology" var with values [nlb, alb, hybrid]. Local testing of resource creation succeeded in dev account. Next: implement canary controller and health aggregation.

2026-02-10 — SRE (Asha Patel): Requested additions to health choreography: require minimum healthy targets per-AZ and integrate with PagerDuty mute during canary window. Also requested metric naming conventions for alerting.

2026-02-22 — Rafael Gomez: Added migration helper script (discover+generate-import). Verified import sequence in staging for a single cluster. Found edge-case when ALB rule priorities collide; added priority relocation helper.

2026-03-03 — QA (Liam O'Connor): Ran streaming load test (5k concurrent). Observed ~1.2% resets when we skipped drain wait; increased default connection_draining_timeout and re-ran — resets dropped to 0.2%.

2026-03-10 — Security (Priya Sharma): Security review started. Flagged that terraform module creates IAM role allowing Describe/Modify for ALB/NLB; requested least-privilege example and explicit terraform provider version pinning. Rafael to address.
notes: Operator runbook must include precise timing guidance: pre-warm targets, wait for cross-AZ health, enable canary at 5% for 10 minutes, then 25/50/100 steps with automated health checks. For TLS passthrough->offload migration, include cert provisioning step and validation of OCSP stapling. Avoid changing session cookie names during cutover to preserve stickiness.
manual_rollback_steps: Invoke canary controller to route 100% traffic back to old target group
If listeners were replaced, re-attach original listener resources via terraform plan -replace and apply
Re-import any lost state using generated import script and rerun terraform apply
Notify on-call and open incident runbook if application errors > 5%
